name: Google Malaysia data center, Elmina Business Park
summary: Google's first data center in Malaysia is being built in Sime Darby Property's Elmina Business Park in Selangor, in Greater Kuala Lumpur. Google announced in May 2024 a US$2 billion investment covering this data center and its first Malaysian cloud region, and broke ground in October 2024. Sime Darby Property is building the facility to Google's specifications under a lease arrangement with Google, which will operate it; Google says it will be water-cooled. Completion was targeted for early 2026, but Google's location list still showed the Selangor site as in development in October 2026.

location.note: Sources name Elmina Business Park in Selangor without an address; the point is the coordinate of the Elmina township from its Wikipedia article, so it marks the township rather than the parcel.

milestones.note: Groundbreaking announced at the Mantap Malaysia Bersama AI event, with the prime minister as guest of honour; EdgeProp reports the ceremony was held in Kuala Lumpur.
Completion was targeted for early 2026; no confirmation of opening was found, and Google still listed the site as in development in October 2026.

notes: Status rests on Google's undated living locations page, which listed Selangor, Malaysia as in development when accessed on 2026-10-09, so status_as_of is the access date. No power capacity was found in a source that could be opened. Wikipedia is cited only for the township coordinate. Google estimates the investment will support about 26,500 jobs across the economy by 2030; that is not a site job count, so it is not recorded as a metric.
